decisions.reason: The dismantling joint is a natural extension of the core pipeline-fitting business, so it likely meets aspirations at low incremental cost and gives no trigger for problemistic search.
The pipe bracket uses existing fabrication and coating capabilities and is cheap to carry in a growing industry, so the firm has no reason to drop it.
The pipe support bracket complements infrastructure projects and draws on existing resources, so it is unlikely to fall short of aspirations enough to justify removal.

The waste bin is distant from the core business and its results are uncertain, but it uses the existing powder-coating capacity and municipal customer contacts, so available slack likely lets the firm carry it a while longer.
The waste bin with ashtray shares production and buyers with Product D, so dropping it would release few resources unless the whole street-furniture line misses aspirations.
The outdoor ashtrays are a diversification with uncertain demand, but the low marginal cost of using existing coating equipment favors keeping the line over a search for alternative uses.
